root_cause: The Postgres dependency is unavailable — either the postgres container was stopped or DB_URL was changed to an invalid value. ShopLite's _db_check() returns False, causing /products and /orders to return HTTP 503, and /health to return HTTP 503 with db=unreachable. The application itself is healthy; only its database dependency has failed.
contributing_factors: FAULT=db_down set, or DB_URL changed to invalid/unreachable host
Postgres container stopped or never started
No connection pooling retry or circuit breaker in the application
Health check also returns 503 so Kubernetes may eventually evict the pod
evidence: Application log: 'Database unreachable — cannot load products'
Application log: 'Database unreachable — cannot persist order'
Postgres pod not running or DB_URL pointing to wrong host

remediation.recommendation: Restore the database connection: restart Postgres and correct DB_URL.
steps: Check Postgres pod/container status: kubectl get pods -n shoplite
If stopped, restart: kubectl rollout restart deployment/postgres -n shoplite
Verify DB_URL in the shoplite-secret points to the correct host and port
Set FAULT=none to clear the injected fault
Add an exponential-backoff retry on DB connection startup to tolerate transient failovers
